title: Routing
summary: Show different pages for different URLs, with path and query parameters.
heading: Routing

blocks.text: A single-page app doesn't reload the whole page when you move around. Instead, the router watches the URL and swaps which component is shown — so each "page" has its own address you can bookmark, share, and use Back/Forward with.
This very app uses the router — each chapter is a route like /chapter/chapter-01.
You define a list of routes — each maps a path to a component — and register them with provideRouter.

Use routerLink instead of href so navigation happens without a full reload. routerLinkActive adds a class to the active link.
A path parameter is part of the URL that changes — like an id. Mark it with : in the route.
Read it from ActivatedRoute. Use the paramMap observable so it updates when the id changes:

blocks.label: product-page.ts

blocks.text: With provideRouter(routes, withComponentInputBinding()) you can skip ActivatedRoute and just declare id = input<string>() — the router feeds the :id straight into the input.
Query parameters are the ?key=value bits after the path — great for things like search terms, filters, or page numbers. They don't need to be declared in the route.

blocks.text: Send the empty path to a default page, and catch anything unknown with a wildcard ** route. Order matters — the wildcard goes last.
